fatal_errors: The proposed entropy-stabilized mechanism is opposite to the observed kinetically controlled, non-sluggish diffusion and surface-energy-driven Au/Cu segregation.
It predicts stability throughout 473–1923 K, whereas the target system becomes unstable above approximately 673 K and undergoes segregation, evaporation, and substantial size loss by 973 K.
It omits the material-specific initial state, including AuCoCuNiPt composition, sub-10 nm size, and FCC multi-twinned/icosahedral morphology.
No controlled comparison or specific heating protocol, atmosphere, particle-size regime, or shape dependence is defined.
The falsification rule is misplaced outside the predicted operating range; degradation within 473–1923 K would be the relevant falsifier.
explanation: The response addresses high-entropy nanoparticles generally but repeats the conventional configurational-entropy stability expectation that the target study disproves. It does not reconstruct vacuum heating to 973 K, the temperature threshold near 673 K, Au/Cu surface segregation, shape-enhanced diffusion, melting/evaporation, loss of 2–4 nm particles, or the reported size reduction. Its cited sources support general HEA definitions and possible bulk or catalytic benefits, not preservation of nanoparticle structure and chemistry over 473–1923 K; E2 even cautions that configurational entropy does not automatically dominate ordering interactions. The proposed experiment is too generic to distinguish entropy stabilization from surface-energy-controlled diffusion because it lacks matched size/shape controls and element-resolved STEM-EDS or diffusivity measurements.
